checks.name: Credential construction
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-policy --offline --test peer credential_construction && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-policy --offline --doc
checks.output: PeerCredential::new(uid, gid, pid) is the only constructor and round-trips all three components ((1000,1000,77) and (0,0,1)). The compile-fail doctest at rust/crates/automonique-policy/src/peer.rs:152 is the crate's single doctest and passes. Its intent was verified rather than assumed: compiling `PeerCredential::default()` against the built rlib with rustc produces error[E0599] 'no function or associated item named `default` found for struct `PeerCredential`', so the doctest fails for the absence of a default constructor and not for an incidental reason. The struct derives Clone/Copy/Debug/Eq/Hash/PartialEq only, so no Default, no From<()> and no ambient-authority constructor exists.

checks.name: Decision totality
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-policy --offline --test peer decision_totality
checks.output: PeerPolicy::evaluate returns Result<Admission, PeerRefusal>, never a boolean and never a collection, so exactly one reason is returned per refusal. evaluate(None) yields CredentialsUnavailable rather than a default admit, and that reason is asserted distinct from UidNotAdmitted both by value and by category. All four reachable refusal reasons were driven through evaluate on one gated policy: CredentialsUnavailable, UidNotAdmitted{uid: 1234}, RootNotAdmitted and GidNotAdmitted{gid: 7}. Admission is constructible only inside evaluate's success arm (its single field is private and it has no public constructor), so there is no path on which an error yields an admission. 23 tests pass in this suite.

checks.name: UID and GID policy
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-policy --offline --test peer uid_and_gid_policy
checks.output: PeerPolicy::new(&[]) fails at construction with NoAdmittedUsers, so a policy admitting nobody cannot exist and there is no wildcard variant to widen into. A policy admitting uid 1000 reports admits_root() == false and refuses uid 0 with RootNotAdmitted; a policy that lists 0 explicitly admits uid 0 and still refuses uid 1000 with UidNotAdmitted. With no group requirement declared, gid 999 is admitted; with requiring_gids(&[42,43]), gid 43 is admitted and gid 44 is refused with GidNotAdmitted{gid: 44}. Duplicate uids in the admitted set are deduplicated and compare equal to the single-entry policy.

checks.name: PID is not authority
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-policy --offline --test peer pid_is_not_authority
checks.output: Six PID values spanning the whole i32 range (i32::MIN, -1, 0, 1, 4242, i32::MAX) produce identical verdicts for the same uid/gid: admitted for uid 1000, UidNotAdmitted{uid: 1234} otherwise. Admission exposes only uid(), so a later stage cannot read a PID back out of the decision. PeerPolicy has no PID field at all (admitted_uids and an optional admitted_gids), so a policy that admits by PID alone is unrepresentable; the nearest constructible expression of it, PeerPolicy::new(&[]), fails at construction with NoAdmittedUsers. The 'fails at construction' clause is therefore satisfied by unrepresentability plus the empty-set refusal, not by a PID-specific constructor error, because no such constructor exists.

checks.name: Mode and ownership
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-policy --offline --test peer mode_and_ownership
checks.output: The three declared requirements are public constants MODE_PRIVATE_DIRECTORY = 0o700, MODE_PRIVATE_FILE = 0o600 and MODE_IMMUTABLE_SPEC = 0o400, and each passes at exactly its own mode. Four more-permissive observations are refused with ModeMorePermissive naming both modes: 0755 against 0700, 0644 and 0666 against 0600, and 0600 against 0400. Two stricter or otherwise-differing observations are refused with ModeMismatch: 0400 against 0600 and 0000 against 0700, so drift is visible in both directions and equal-or-stricter is not silently accepted. An entry owned by uid 0 where 1000 is expected is refused with UnexpectedOwner{expected: 1000, observed: 0}. All inputs are caller-supplied EntryMetadata values; no filesystem is touched.

checks.name: Path safety
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-policy --offline --test peer path_safety
checks.output: Each rule refuses with its own category: symlinked component -> symlink_component, group- or world-writable parent -> writable_parent, wrong owner -> unexpected_owner (via check_entry); embedded NUL -> embedded_nul, absolute path -> absolute_path, empty string and empty or '.' components -> non_canonical_path, and '../../etc/passwd' and 'hosts/../../etc/passwd' -> path_escape (via check_relative_path). Four canonical runtime-relative paths are accepted. Every rule is evaluated over the supplied string or metadata alone, with no filesystem call, so it holds before any syscall and cannot be defeated by a race. Recorded honestly: check_relative_path accepts an in-root '..' segment ('hosts/h-1/nested/../sibling' is in the accepted list), so 'non-canonical traversal' is enforced for empty and '.' components and for escapes above the root, but a path that traverses upward and back down within the root is admitted rather than refused.

checks.name: Refusal hygiene
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-policy --offline --test peer refusal_hygiene
checks.output: All 13 PeerRefusal variants are enumerated, matched exhaustively (a new variant is a compile error) and have 13 distinct categories after dedup: credentials_unavailable, uid_not_admitted, root_not_admitted, gid_not_admitted, mode_more_permissive, mode_mismatch, unexpected_owner, symlink_component, writable_parent, embedded_nul, absolute_path, path_escape, non_canonical_path. Every one of the 13 is also reached through a public function elsewhere in the suite (evaluate for the first four, check_entry for the next three, check_relative_path for the last six), so no category is reachable only by hand-constructing the variant. Refusals built from a synthetic socket path '/run/user/1000/automonique/hosts/h-1/control.sock' and a synthetic command line '/usr/bin/curl --header authorization:secret' render without containing either string or the substring 'secret'; no variant carries anything beyond numeric ids and mode bits.
